title: 88 couples say 'I do' together in Nuevo Laredo's seventh collective wedding campaign
excerpt: Eighty-eight couples formalized their unions in Nuevo Laredo's seventh collective wedding campaign, run by the city DIF system with the Tamaulipas Civil Registry. Since October 2021, 633 couples have married through the program.
content:
Eighty-eight couples formalized their unions together in Nuevo Laredo's seventh Campaña de Matrimonios Colectivos, the city's DIF family-services system announced.

The collective wedding campaign was carried out by the Sistema DIF Nuevo Laredo in coordination with the Registro Civil de Tamaulipas, as part of efforts to promote the well-being and stability of families in the city. The couples married in a single shared ceremony rather than in separate civil proceedings.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal and DIF Nuevo Laredo president Claudette Canturosas Villarreal backed the campaign, which removes cost and paperwork barriers that can keep couples from formalizing unions they have already built their lives around.

A program that keeps growing

Since October 2021, 633 couples have formalized their unions through the DIF's collective wedding campaigns. The seventh edition's 88 couples continue a steady run of ceremonies that give families legal recognition — and the rights that come with it, from inheritance and hospital decisions to registering children and accessing family benefits.

For many couples, a civil marriage is not about the ceremony. It is about paperwork that protects a family: a spouse's right to make medical decisions, to inherit, to be recognized on official documents. Collective campaigns handle the legal process in bulk, at no cost to the couples, so that money is not the reason a family stays informal.

Why it matters on both sides of the river

Nuevo Laredo and Laredo share families, not just a border. A marriage formalized in Nuevo Laredo is a legal fact that follows a couple wherever they live and work — including across the river, where binational families navigate two legal systems at once. Programs like this one are a reminder that the most important civic work is often the quietest: paperwork, done together, for families who asked for it.

Webb Watch 956 will keep covering the community programs that make life in the two Laredos a little more secure — on both sides of the Rio Grande.
